title: Tagline dataLayer contract
description: Every object or gtag() command the Tagline Supply site pushes to window.dataLayer. Validate any push against the root: arrays are gtag() commands (normalise the Arguments object with Array.from first), objects with an `event` key are events, objects without one are the ecommerce clear or the user_id push. Human-readable version: docs/tagging-plan.md. Event names and parameters follow Google's GA4 recommended events reference and the GTM ecommerce dataLayer format; where this contract is stricter than Google, the plan lists it under Deviations.
$comment: Contract version 1.0.0 (Stage 1). Change this file, docs/tagging-plan.md and the site's tests in the same pull request. Every object is closed (additionalProperties: false) so a typo or a stray key fails loudly instead of leaking into GTM's merged data model; the only exception is keys starting with `gtm.`, which Google's own libraries write into the dataLayer. Ajv 2020 with strict: true compiles this schema without warnings.

data_push.description: Dispatcher: an object push. With an `event` key it is an event; without one it is the ecommerce clear or the user_id push.

event_push.description: Dispatcher: events. `gtm.*` events belong to Google's libraries and are tolerated; every other event must be one of event_name.

tagline_event.description: Dispatcher: routes each event name to its $defs entry. An unknown name fails on the enum.

state_push.description: Dispatcher: object pushes without an event. `{ user_id }` sets or clears identity; anything else must be exactly `{ ecommerce: null }`.

gtag_command.description: Dispatcher: a gtag() call, i.e. the Arguments object the standard shim `function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}` pushes, normalised to an array. Consent commands are always present; js/config/set/event appear only when GA4 forwarding is on.

event_name.description: The 14 events in the contract: 13 GA4 recommended events plus page_view. GA4 can collect page views on its own, even in a single-page app; the site pushes page_view itself so each page's events have one in front of them in the dataLayer, and GA4's own history-based page views are turned off when forwarding. Adding an event means a new $defs entry, a row in the plan and a builder test.

looks_like_email.description: Used under `not`: an email address, raw or URL-encoded (@ or %40). Google's PII policy forbids sending one in any parameter.

text.description: A non-empty string within GA4's 100-character limit for event parameter values.

absolute_url.description: A full URL with protocol, no fragment (GA4 drops the fragment by default and the site uses path-based routes) and no email address in it.

pseudonymous_id.description: The user_id: 32 lowercase hex characters, an opaque account id (128 random bits issued per account, not derived from the email). The pattern guarantees no raw email, name or username is sent; that the id is random is a code rule (site/src/auth/accounts.ts), not something a pattern can check. The email itself never enters the dataLayer.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the event's money values. Tagline prices everything in US dollars, so the only valid value is USD.

value.description: Σ price × quantity over the event's items, before tax and shipping. A number, never a string. The site sums in integer cents, so it has at most 2 decimals; this schema checks only that it is a positive number, and the unit tests check the arithmetic and the cents.

item_list_id.description: Stable machine id of a product list, snake_case, e.g. all_products, category_drinkware, search_results.

item_list_name.description: Human-readable name of the same list, e.g. Drinkware.

item.description: One product line in an ecommerce event: the GA4 item parameters Tagline sends. Closed: Google allows up to 27 custom item parameters, this contract allows none.

item_id.description: Catalog SKU: TL-<3-letter category code>-<3 digits>.

price.description: Unit price in USD, > 0. Catalog prices have at most 2 decimals; the catalog unit test checks that, this schema does not.

quantity.description: Units. On add_to_cart and remove_from_cart: the units added or removed by this action, not the new line total.

index.description: 0-based position in the list the item was shown in. Required in list events, allowed elsewhere.

list_item.description: An item shown in a product list: an item with a required index.

items_cart.description: One or more items; GA4 accepts up to 200 per event.

items_listed.description: One or more list items; GA4 accepts up to 200 per event.

page_view.title: page_view
page_view.description: One virtual page view per page visit, including the first load: a new history entry, Back/Forward, or a replace that changes the URL. Never per re-render, and not for a click on a link to the page already shown (react-router turns that into a replace to the same URL).

page_location.description: Full URL of the page. GA4 limit 1,000 characters.

page_title.description: document.title after the route has set it. GA4 limit 300 characters.

page_referrer.description: Previous page_location on in-app navigation; document.referrer on the first load when it is non-empty. Omitted, never empty, when unknown. GA4 limit 420 characters.

view_item_list.title: view_item_list
view_item_list.description: A product list rendered with at least one product (home, category filter, search results). Once per list per page view.

select_item.title: select_item
select_item.description: A product in a list was clicked. Same list id and name as the view_item_list it came from, one item with its index.

view_item.title: view_item
view_item.description: Product detail page shown for a known product. value = price × 1.

add_to_cart.title: add_to_cart
add_to_cart.description: Units of one product added to the cart. items[0].quantity = units added; value = price × units added.

remove_from_cart.title: remove_from_cart
remove_from_cart.description: Units of one product removed from the cart by the user. items[0].quantity = units removed; value = price × units removed.

view_cart.title: view_cart
view_cart.description: Cart page shown with at least one line. Every line in items; value = cart subtotal.

begin_checkout.title: begin_checkout
begin_checkout.description: Checkout page entered with a non-empty cart.

add_shipping_info.title: add_shipping_info
add_shipping_info.description: The user chose a shipping tier. value excludes the shipping cost.

add_payment_info.title: add_payment_info
add_payment_info.description: The user chose a payment type. No payment details exist anywhere in the site.

purchase.title: purchase
purchase.description: Order confirmed. Exactly once per transaction_id: a reload, back/forward or revisit of the confirmation page must not push it again. value excludes tax and shipping, which have their own params.

transaction_id.description: Order id: TL-<base36 timestamp>-<base36 random>. Unique per order, never empty (GA4 deduplicates every purchase with transaction_id "" into one), no customer data in it.

shipping.description: Shipping cost in USD; 0 is valid.

search.title: search
search.description: A search was submitted with a non-empty term. Fires on submit, even when there are no results.

search_term.description: The term as typed: trimmed, whitespace collapsed, any email address replaced by [email], cut to 100 characters.

login.title: login
login.description: An existing account signed in. Preceded by the { user_id } push; user_id itself is never an event parameter.

sign_up.title: sign_up
sign_up.description: A new account was created (and is now signed in). Preceded by the { user_id } push. A sign-up does not also push login.

ecommerce_clear.title: ecommerce: null
ecommerce_clear.description: Pushed immediately before every ecommerce event so GTM's data model never merges a stale ecommerce object into the next event.

set_user_id.title: user_id
set_user_id.description: Identity push. A pseudonymous id on sign-in (and on app start while signed in, before the first page_view); null on sign-out. Never an empty string or the string "null" (Google). Never pushed for a visitor who has not signed in.

google_internal_event.title: gtm.*
google_internal_event.description: Messages Google's own libraries push (for example the GTM snippet's { event: 'gtm.js', 'gtm.start': … }). Tolerated, not described: only gtm.* keys are allowed next to event.

gtag_consent.title: gtag consent
gtag_consent.description: Consent Mode v2. gtag('consent', 'default', …) is the first dataLayer entry on every load; gtag('consent', 'update', …) follows on Accept/Reject or when a stored choice is re-applied.

gtag_consent_default.description: ['consent', 'default', {...}]: all four v2 consent types set, all denied, and nothing else.

gtag_consent_update.description: ['consent', 'update', {...}]: all four v2 consent types, each granted or denied. The banner's Accept sets all four granted, Reject all four denied.

gtag_js.description: ['js', Date]: part of the gtag.js snippet. The second item is a Date (an ISO string once JSON-cloned).

gtag_config.description: ['config', 'G-…', { send_page_view: false }]: GA4 forwarding only. send_page_view must be false because the site sends its own page_view per page. user_id goes through set, not config.

gtag_set.description: ['set', {...}]: GA4 forwarding only, in one of two forms. { user_id }: Google's recommended way to set user_id after the tag has loaded, and to clear it with null on sign-out. { page_location, page_title, page_referrer }: the cleaned values of the page_view about to be forwarded, so every later hit on the page, including the ones gtag.js sends on its own, uses them instead of the raw document.location.

gtag_event.description: ['event', name, params]: GA4 forwarding only, a copy of an event already validated as a dataLayer push (ecommerce fields flattened into params, as gtag.js expects). Checked here: the name, and that no gtm.* key rides along (gtag.js would send it as a junk ep.gtm parameter).
